utility.notes: PG&E's own electric service territory map covers all of San Mateo County. Millbrae is a well-documented San Mateo County city, consistent with PG&E service already established for other San Mateo County records this session.

value.name: WestLight Energy (formerly Peninsula Clean Energy) - ECOplus (default)
value.notes: Confirmed directly via WestLight Energy's own site, which states it serves San Mateo County (including Millbrae) and the City of Los Banos, with ECOplus remaining the default product (50% renewable, rates effective July 1, 2026, lower than PG&E). PG&E continues to handle billing, metering, and outage response. The City of Millbrae's own civic-alert page previously cited for this rebrand (CivicAlerts.aspx?AID=164) returned a confirmed 404 on re-check; searching the City's current site found no live replacement page documenting this specific rebrand (the City's own 'Energy Conservation' page, ci.millbrae.ca.us/337/Energy-Conservation, is itself stale and still links to the pre-rebrand peninsulacleanenergy.com domain rather than westlightenergy.org). Rather than cite a dead or non-corroborating page, this fact is now supported solely by WestLight Energy's own official site, which independently and currently confirms Millbrae/San Mateo County coverage.

interconnection_url.notes: PG&E's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other PG&E-territory records in this dataset.

value.name: California SGIP - current category and budget check required
value.description: New applications and waitlist applications for ratepayer-funded SGIP budgets closed on December 30, 2025. New AB 209 applications have a June 30, 2028 deadline. The 2026 SGIP rate table publishes $3.10/W for solar and $1.10/Wh for storage in applicable Residential Solar and Storage Equity categories. Household eligibility and live budget availability vary by category and program administrator; check the official Program Metrics tracker before relying on an incentive.
value.eligibility: Eligibility varies by 2026 SGIP budget category, program administrator, property, income/pathway, project rules, and live funding availability.

battery_programs.notes: SGIP program data refreshed on 2026-08-26 from the official 2026 Handbook and live Program Metrics. Earlier locality records contained 2025 opening/availability language. This record does not assert household eligibility, reservation availability, or a guaranteed incentive; current category and program-administrator status must be checked before reliance.

required_documents.notes: The city references a 'Structural Criteria for Residential Flush-Mounted Solar Arrays' handout on its Forms & Other Handouts page, but its specific content was not independently read this session (a widely-reused statewide-template document also seen at other cities, so its Millbrae-specific applicability was not separately confirmed).

value: Call the Building Division at 650-259-2330 to schedule an inspection
Inspections are conducted Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to noon and 1:00 p.m. to 4:30 p.m.
inspection_steps.notes: This is the City's general Building Division inspection scheduling process (the same page covers all building permit types, including solar); the City's page does not describe a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.

value.notes: The city's Building Division page states 'Permit applicants should allow 15 days for all plan check activities to be performed' as the standard timeline; solar PV systems are separately described as qualifying for a streamlined, in-house expedited review, which the source suggests may be faster than the standard 15-day timeline but does not itself quantify.

value.program_or_pathway: Streamlined in-house review for SolarPV systems
other_conditions: The city's own page states: 'Certain types of permits may be subject to a streamlined permitting process and will be reviewed in-house as time allows, these permits/plans are typically for SolarPV systems, kitchen, and bath remodels'
